# Reward-ranked next ten global targets

## Ranking principle

The ordering favors targets that either instantiate the first missing physical
object or kill a major remaining shortcut.  A target is complete only when its
quantifiers, arithmetic status, hostile tests, dependency JSON, and claim-level
ledger are explicit.

The audit hygiene items have been closed: H7-F5 now uses distinct signed chart
coordinates and a hostile transition test; H2's additive corollary includes
the homogeneous-rate hypothesis; H1/H2/H5 distinguish algebraic identities
from tolerance-certified computations; and H6 explicitly limits its exact
operator claim to the displayed hashed rational fixture.  These repairs
improve reliability but do not move the physical frontier by themselves.

## 1. Minimal same-measure nonlinear `SU(2)` retained kernel

**Reward:** maximal.  This is the first physical blocker shared by every
stream.

Construct the smallest nontrivial one- or two-block lattice example in which
the Gibbs conditional law, temporal transfer, retained boundary state,
normalized kernel, and bad event all come from the same nonlinear `SU(2)`
measure.  Record gauge invariance, normalization, positivity/reflection
positivity, boundary-history domain, and exact volume/cutoff dependencies.

**Exit criterion:** a normalized kernel and transfer operator with no
independently chosen toy mask or surrogate measure; otherwise a precise
no-go/obstruction theorem.

## 2. Same-measure full-spectrum observability/coercivity

**Reward:** maximal.  Stage 68 proves this gate cannot be replaced by defect
rarity.

Define a gauge-invariant defect observable on the Target 1 kernel and seek an
inequality controlling every nonvacuum temporal mode, not only the visible
masked channel.  Test hidden low modes and multiplicity directions using the
H9 criterion.

**Exit criterion:** a finite nonlinear coercivity theorem with explicit
constant and nullspace, or a countermodel locating the missing observable.

## 3. Uniform normalization, chart mass, and root-weight moment

**Reward:** very high.  This is the quantitative bottleneck connecting H1 and
H7 to iteration.

For every declared positive-mass boundary history, bound chart normalizers,
exceptional amplification, and the inverse-vacuum root moment on the same
kernel.  Track volume and lattice spacing explicitly and fail closed at zero
chart mass.

**Exit criterion:** a boundary-history-uniform theorem on a growing finite
family, or an explicit family proving which retained variable is missing.

## 4. Physical bad/good partition ratio or quasi-factorization

**Reward:** very high.  It converts energetic intuition into a normalized
probability statement.

Derive `Z_bad/Z_good` for the actual constrained conditional measure, including
entropy/multiplicity and interaction corrections.  In parallel, test whether a
positive interacting defect quasi-factorization constant can hold under a
specific mixing hypothesis.

**Exit criterion:** a strict uniform ratio on the Target 1 family, or a sharp
counterexample identifying the necessary mixing/coercivity input.

## 5. Complete retained state: topology, refinement, and observables

**Reward:** high.  An incomplete state invalidates both gluing and density.

Combine a bounded relative/interface topology carrier (H4), certified stable
refinement (H8), and a separating product-closed invariant observable algebra
(H10).  Prefer intrinsic gauge-invariant data; if charts are unavoidable,
prove controlled transitions.

**Exit criterion:** exact gluing closure and exact recovery on a nonlinear
finite `SU(2)` block, plus a complexity bound better than explicit exponential
enumeration.

## 6. Growing-family nonlinear repair law

**Reward:** high.  H3 currently proves collectivity only on one fixed complex.

Construct a growing block/polymer family, characterize its repair-relevant bad
displacement cone, and prove that collective zero- or low-spill directions
cover that cone with controlled Jacobian, multiplicity, topology, and boundary
trace.

**Exit criterion:** a size-indexed theorem with constants and boundary law, not
another isolated finite spectrum.

## 7. Gauge-covariant typed multiscale square with stable recovery

**Reward:** high.  This turns the H6 calculus into a physical transport tool.

Instantiate the typed square for the nonlinear kernel and retained state.
Prove positive or reflection-positive recovery, support-indexed seminorm
bounds, future invariance/contraction, and repeated-scale summability.  Include
an explicit typed provenance map from the repair operator.

**Exit criterion:** a growing exact or rigorously enclosed tower with a uniform
recovered-defect budget.

## 8. Tempered atlas and observable-growth theorem in physical length

**Reward:** medium-high.  It prevents representational changes from
manufacturing the desired exponent.

Control the H2 endpoint coboundary, cumulative projective width, homogeneous
product, injected-error budget, and H10 observable reconstruction/support norm
relative to accumulated physical length.  Distinguish scalar gauge
renormalization from state-dependent distortion.

**Exit criterion:** all distortion terms are sublinear in physical length and
the surviving rate remains strictly positive uniformly in cutoff.

## 9. Continuum OS construction with a dense gauge-invariant temporal core

**Reward:** maximal but downstream.  It supplies the space on which the final
spectral statement is meaningful.

Construct compatible Schwinger functions or measures, prove the required OS
axioms and theory identity, and show that the recovered gauge-invariant
temporal observable class is dense in the OS norm, including all spectral
multiplicities.

**Exit criterion:** a nontrivial continuum pure Yang--Mills Hilbert space with
a named dense temporal core and justified limit interchanges.

## 10. Uniform decay-to-gap closure and Clay quantifiers

**Reward:** terminal.  Attempt only after Targets 1--9 have supplied their
hypotheses.

Transfer the physical-length decay to the dense OS core, extend it to the full
vacuum-orthogonal Hilbert space, and apply the spectral theorem.  Then audit
existence, locality, covariance, positivity, nontriviality, group dependence,
and the exact Clay quantifiers.

**Exit criterion:** a C5/C6-quality theorem with every regulator, volume,
observable, physical-time, and compact-simple-group quantifier explicit.  If
any prerequisite remains conditional, retain C3 and state the first missing
implication.

## Run-wide claim discipline

For every target, report separately:

- finite exact, interval-certified, or floating-tolerance evidence;
- restricted theorem versus conditional physical bridge;
- all boundary, volume, cutoff, history, scale, support, and observable
  quantifiers;
- the first unproved implication;
- whether the object is the actual nonlinear Yang--Mills conditional measure;
- whether the decay is per RG step or per physical time.

No target may infer a temporal gap from a weighted defect or partition ratio
without Target 2, or infer a full gap from a visible core without Target 9.
